BIM Staffing vs BIM Outsourcing: Which Is Better?

Staffing adds people you direct; outsourcing hands over a defined package. The right choice depends on who should own the model, the standards and the risk.

When a project needs more BIM capacity than the in-house team has, there are two broad routes. You can add people to your team (BIM staffing), or you can hand a defined piece of work to a provider who delivers it (BIM outsourcing of a package). Both work. They fail for different reasons, so the decision is worth making deliberately.

What each model means in practice

BIM staffing places BIM professionals inside your team, onsite or remotely. They work in your common data environment, to your BIM Execution Plan and templates, and your BIM manager or project lead directs them day to day. The provider is responsible for sourcing, assessing and supporting the person; you are responsible for the work they produce.

Package outsourcing gives a scope to a provider: model the MEP services for levels 1 to 20 to LOD 350, produce the shop drawings, or run the clash detection cycle. The provider manages its own people and delivers the outputs to an agreed standard and date. You review and accept deliverables rather than directing individuals.

Five questions that decide it

1. Who should own the model day to day?

If design decisions change weekly and your team must steer the model closely, staffing keeps control in-house. If the scope is stable and well defined, outsourcing lets you manage outputs instead of people.

2. How mature are your standards?

Staffed professionals follow your standards, so those standards must exist. A provider delivering a package can work to your BEP, but it can also bring its own checklists when yours are thin.

3. Where does the risk sit?

With staffing, quality risk stays largely with you; the provider carries the risk of the person being suitable and replaced if not. With a package, delivery risk moves to the provider, within the limits of the scope.

4. How long is the need?

Ongoing or open-ended needs suit staffing, including long-term placements. A defined deliverable with an end date suits a package.

5. How much management time do you have?

Staffed engineers need direction. If your BIM manager is already stretched, a dedicated team with its own lead or a package may be the better use of their time.

A common middle ground

Many projects combine the two: a coordinator staffed onsite to run meetings and decisions, with modelling delivered as a package or by a remote team. What matters is that one BEP, one CDE and one clash process apply to everyone.

How ENGISOFT approaches it

ENGISOFT offers both BIM staffing and BIM services, so the recommendation does not depend on which one we sell. In a first conversation we usually ask the five questions above and suggest the model that fits the project rather than a default.
